47d863da95953d2e.h:
Self-defense law · stand your ground

District of Columbia

Middle ground: no duty to retreat, but whether one could have retreated may be weighed

Washington, D.C. adopts a "middle ground" approach, under which "The law does not require a person to retreat," but "in deciding whether [defendant] reasonably at the time of the incident believed that s/he was in imminent danger of death or serious bodily harm and that deadly force was necessary to repel that danger, you may consider, along with any other evidence, whether the [defendant] could have safely retreated ... but did not."

Wikipedia, "Stand-your-ground law", United States section and its map legend (text CC BY-SA 4.0), read 17 October 2026. The article cites Westlaw pattern jury instructions, state statutes and case law for each state.
47d863da95953d2e.t: District of Columbia · Middle ground: no duty to retreat, but whether one could have retreated may be weighed

757ff2e4ee9d9e80.h:
Self-defense law · stand your ground

Wisconsin

Middle ground: no duty to retreat, but whether one could have retreated may be weighed

Wisconsin also adopts a "middle ground" approach, where "while there is no statutory duty to retreat, whether the opportunity to retreat was available goes to whether the defendant reasonably believed the force used was necessary to prevent an interference with his or her person." In Wisconsin and Guam, the duty to retreat does not apply when the defender is in the defender's vehicle, nor in the workplace if the defender is its owner or operator.

Has a law providing civil immunity under certain self-defense circumstances.

710d141d6ea67bcf.h:
Self-defense law · stand your ground

Guam

Duty to retreat, except in one's home, vehicle or workplace (workplace only for its owner or operator)

In Wisconsin and Guam, the duty to retreat also does not apply when the defender is in the defender's vehicle; the same is true of the place of work, but only if the defender is the owner or operator of the workplace.

In all duty-to-retreat states, the duty to retreat does not apply when the defender is in the defender's home (except, in some jurisdictions, when defending against a fellow occupant of that home): the castle doctrine. Here the duty applies only when one can retreat with absolute safety.

432cecd470b8ac3c.h:
Self-defense law · duty to retreat

Canada

In Canada, there is no duty to retreat under the law. Canada's laws regarding self-defence are similar in nature to those of England, as they centre around the acts committed, and whether those acts are considered reasonable in the circumstances. Generally where retreat is available in the circumstances, the decision to stand your ground is more likely to be unreasonable. The sections of the Canadian criminal code that deal with self-defence or defence of property are sections 34 and 35, respectively. In Ontario, jurors are not permitted "...to consider whether an accused could have retreated from his or her own home in the face of an attack (or threatened attack) by an assailant in assessing the elements of self-defence." In British Columbia, courts will permit juries to consider available lines of retreat in deciding whether an accused had no other option than to defend himself; the option of retreat is not considered a categorical exclusion from self-defence.

Self-defense law · duty to retreat

Czech Republic

Czech law abandoned the duty to retreat in 1852. Since then, the successive recodifications of criminal law lacked any such requirement. In order for a defense to be judged as legitimate, it may not be "manifestly disproportionate to the manner of the attack".

2b38c86b6aa292e4.h:
Self-defense law · duty to retreat

England and Wales

The common law jurisdiction of England and Wales has a stand-your-ground law rooted in the common law defense of using reasonable force in self-defense. There is no duty to retreat before a person may use reasonable force against an attacker, but one who chooses not to retreat, when retreat would be a safe and easy option, might find it harder to justify his use of force as 'reasonable'. In the home, force used against an intruder is not to be regarded as reasonable if it is 'grossly disproportionate'.

651bfa3c4c49babe.h:
Self-defense law · duty to retreat

France

Under article 122-5 of the French Criminal Code, a person who, faced with an unjustified attack on himself or another, performs an act required by the need for self-defense is not criminally responsible, unless there is a disproportion between the means of defense used and the seriousness of the attack. There is no duty to retreat. A person is presumed to have acted in self-defense when repelling, by night, entry by break-in, violence or trickery into an inhabited place, or when defending against robbery or looting executed with violence.

7548d9598b43280f.h:
Self-defense law · duty to retreat

Germany

German law permits self-defense against an unlawful attack. If there is no other possibility for defense, it is generally allowed to use even deadly force without a duty to retreat. However, there must not be an extreme imbalance ("extremes Missverhältnis") between the defended right and the chosen method of defense. If the self-defense was excessive, its perpetrator is not to be punished if he or she exceeded on account of confusion, fear or terror.

c8fd9f95a664d3f7.h:
Self-defense law · duty to retreat

Ireland

Under the Criminal Law (Defence and the Dwelling) Act 2011, property owners or residents are entitled to defend themselves with force, up to and including lethal force, against a trespasser they honestly believe was there to commit a criminal act and a threat to life, provided another reasonable person in the same circumstances would likely react the same way. The law was introduced in response to DPP v. Padraig Nally.

Self-defense law · duty to retreat

Poland

Stand-your-ground law applies to any kind of threat by an attacker that endangers the victim's safety, health, or life. The victim has no obligation to retreat (Supreme Court of Poland, 4 February 1972). Section 2a of the Polish Penal Code, introduced in 2017, codifies a limited castle doctrine, excluding punishment for excessive force while protecting one's home unless exceeding the limits of necessary defense was gross.

a3af4f37bc9ce1a9.h:
Self-defense law · duty to retreat

Alberta, Canada

The province of Alberta is unique among Canadian jurisdictions in affording civil immunity to occupiers who employ force, including lethal force, in defense of homes and other premises. In 2019, the Alberta legislature passed the Trespass Statutes (Protecting Law-Abiding Property Owners) Amendment Act, 2019, amending the Occupiers' Liability Act: where a trespasser is a criminal trespasser, no action lies against the occupier for damages for death of or injury to the trespasser unless the conduct is wilful and grossly disproportionate and results in a conviction prosecuted by indictment.
